chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Aban ibn Uthman, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the mute woman. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wrap her veil upon her head and pull it away.'

key_terms.الْخَرْسَاءِ: The mute woman (one who cannot speak)

ai.seo_question: How is a divorce validly executed for a mute woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the mechanism for divorcing a mute woman (kharsa') by using the physical removal of her veil as a clear, observable sign of consent, compensating for her inability to speak. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of relying on unambiguous physical indicators (ishara) when verbal communication is absent, ensuring the validity of the divorce without requiring complex interpretive assumptions.
